facts.text: Tobin Hill was originally called the Old Main Association, a name that dates back to its 1731 founding.
The neighborhood covers roughly 700 acres just north of downtown San Antonio, a sizable suburban enclave.
Its borders run from Huisache Avenue in the north to Interstate 35 in the south, Broadway to the east, and San Pedro Avenue to the west.
Development kicked off in 1877 when Colonel Augustus Belknap built a horse railroad from Houston Street to San Pedro Springs Park.
Although land was distributed by lottery as early as 1777, actual settlement didn’t begin until the late 19th century.
Tobin Hill’s streets follow a planned rectilinear subdivision, a design choice highlighted by the Texas Center for Landscape Architecture.
